key_insight: BridgeTwist turns a pretrained Schrödinger bridge into a training-free conditional sampler by twisting the bridge with a likelihood-based surrogate and time-varying tempering.
engineering_relevance: This gives a reusable inference-time way to adapt one generative model to many downstream conditional tasks without retraining.
method: Builds a plug-in twist from the SB velocity and score fields to predict endpoints and score the task likelihood there.
Uses a time-varying exponent to weaken the twist near the source where the surrogate is least reliable.
Adds a bridge-shaped diffusion schedule and importance weighting so intermediate twist factors telescope away.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on class-conditional and text-prompted image generation, and on inverse problems including inpainting, deblurring, and super-resolution, where it outperforms training-free baselines and is competitive with specialized solvers.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the endpoint surrogate and the chosen tempering/schedule, especially early in the bridge where the twist is least accurate.
paper_title: BridgeTwist: Twisting Schrödinger Bridges for Training-Free Conditional Sampling
